title: Who Writes What: Unveiling the Impact of Author Roles on AI-generated Text Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing AI text detection accuracy on human-authored and parallel LLM-generated texts across different CEFR language proficiency levels (A2, B1, B2, Native) using multi-factor Weighted Least Squares (WLS) regression and Type II ANOVA.

Evaluating differences in AI text detection accuracy across texts from diverse language environments (Native Speakers, English as a Foreign Language, and English as a Second Language) using multi-factor ANOVA and post-hoc pairwise comparisons.

Measuring variations in AI text detection accuracy between texts written by (or prompted to emulate) male versus female authors, utilizing multi-factor WLS regression to control for other confounding variables.

Analyzing AI text detection accuracy across different academic fields (Sciences & Technology, Social Sciences, Humanities, Life Sciences) to determine if disciplinary writing norms influence misclassification rates.
